messages.subject: Shiny-server "Could not open session"

An error has occurred

could not open session

messages.subject: Re: Shiny-server "Could not open session"
parts:
This seems to indicate that the Shiny app was launched but exited immediately. The error message doesn't seem to originate from the Shiny package itself. Can you think of any of your R code that would cause this error?

If not, can you try sprinkling calls like this:

cat("Got here 1\n", file=stderr())

cat("Got here 2\n", file=stderr())

around suspicious parts of your R code and see which ones show up in the browser when the error page is shown?

messages.author: c620544f71224624
messages.subject: Re: Shiny-server "Could not open session"
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply. I sprinkled some comments around, but got nothing in the log file. 

I've had some problems with this "box", which is a corporate hosted VM. I might have better luck with another machine. Here are a few thoughts about what might be causing the problem:

* I added the system user, and the user exists, but perhaps I should have IT create a user under Windows AD.
* I am currently using a VPN connection. But I'm using the same connection for RStudio, which works fine.
* I have multiple versions of R stored on this box, all built from source. Maybe shiny is not pointing to the right place.
* Installed node under python26, but then reverted back to python24. I've tested this bug using both versions of python, and it doesn't seem to make a difference.
* X11 continues to give me problems on this box. But I tend to think that is a separate issue.

That's a lot of dirty laundry. I think I'll have the most success trying another box at this point.

--Nathan

parts: "I added the system user, and the user exists, but perhaps I should have IT create a user under Windows AD"

This sounds the most suspicious to me. Can you try running the following:

sudo su - shiny

(assuming that the username is shiny)

If that fails with the same error message, then it does sound like creating a user under Windows AD might help.
